questions.q: How does the chapter describe its three categories of burnout, spiritual dryness and emotional overload?
options: As pastoral descriptions that overlap and are not diagnoses
As clinical diagnoses a reader can apply to themselves
As three stages that always follow one another
As signs of hidden sin
questions.explanation: The author writes as a pastor experienced in counselling, not a doctor. Some signs overlap with depression, anxiety, chronic stress and physical illness, which is why Chapter 5 matters.

questions.q: When Moses said the burden was too heavy for him (Numbers 11:10–15), how did God respond?
options: He rebuked Moses for weak faith
He shared the burden among seventy elders
He told Moses to pray harder and try again
He removed Moses from leadership
questions.explanation: The remedy was structural, shared responsibility (Numbers 11:16–17), just as Jethro had earlier warned Moses that judging alone would wear him out (Exodus 18:13–23).

questions.q: According to the chapter, what is the central difficulty in burnout?
options: God feels distant even when life is calm
Too much emotion to process at once
Prolonged demands with inadequate recovery or support
A lack of spiritual gifts
questions.explanation: Burnout is deep exhaustion from pouring out for far longer than you have been receiving rest, help, encouragement or care. Rest alone will not cure it if the structure that emptied you stays the same.

questions.q: What does the chapter say about the cause of spiritual dryness?
options: It is always the result of unconfessed sin
It is never connected to sin
It is caused by too much prayer
It is not always the result of sin; sometimes there is something to confess (Psalm 32), but often, as with Job, there is nothing to find
questions.explanation: Psalms 42, 63 and 13 show people holding on to faith while feeling nothing. Scripture preserved those prayers so we would know the experience is not unusual.

questions.q: Which of these is listed as a common sign of emotional overload?
options: Crying, or being close to it, without an obvious trigger
Increasing cynicism toward the people you serve
Wondering whether earlier experiences of God were real
Dreading ministry you used to find meaningful
questions.explanation: Overloaded people often look fine, but the weight shows in unexpected tears, disproportionate reactions to small things and a flatness that has replaced both joy and sorrow. The other options belong to the burnout and dryness lists.

questions.q: When does the chapter say a pastoral description stops being adequate and a doctor or mental-health professional should be consulted?
options: Only after a full year of difficulty
When low mood, emptiness or loss of interest has been present most days for two weeks or longer, or is significantly affecting daily functioning
Never, because a retreat is enough
Only if a pastor recommends it
questions.explanation: You do not need to wait until things become severe. And anyone with thoughts of not wanting to be alive should tell a trusted person and contact a professional or crisis service promptly.

reflection: Which of the three descriptions had the most marks: burnout, spiritual dryness, or emotional overload? Which had the fewest?
How long has this been going on? Weeks, months, or longer? When did you first notice?
Is there a specific event you can connect it to (a loss, a move, a conflict, a change of role), or did it build gradually with no obvious cause?

Did the section "Where this stops being pastoral" describe you? If so, what support do you need today? Write the name of the person, doctor, counsellor, crisis service, or emergency service you will contact.
